Interactions.description: A press on one of this message's Buttons (or a control in its Blocks): `await msg-[:Interactions]->` waits for the next one, and `listen to chat-[:Channels]->-[m:Messages WHERE m.Topic == "lunch-poll"]->-[:Interactions]->` runs once per press on any message written with that Topic.

Reactions.description: React to this message with an emoji, or hear a reaction added: `listen to chat-[ch:Channels WHERE ch.Name == "deals"]->-[:Messages]->-[:Reactions]->`. A reaction arrives with its channel, not its message, so a listen narrows it by channel; reading a message's reactions back is not offered (a call per message).

Message.description: A Slack message — what a listen on a channel's `Messages` delivers, whole: read `m.Message` straight off it, reply along its `Replies` edge, react to it along its `Reactions` edge. Created only along an edge: post via a Channel's `Messages` edge, reply via a message's `Replies` edge — the channel and thread come from the parent, never from fields.

fieldDocs.Id: Names this message in its workspace: its channel's id and its Slack timestamp (`C…:1700000000.000100`).
fieldDocs.Message: The message body. Required unless a File is attached or Blocks are set (at least one of Message / File / Blocks). Use Slack-native formatting (*bold*, _italic_, <url|text>).
fieldDocs.File: Optional file to upload with the message — the Message text rides as the file caption, one visible Slack message. Send-side only: a received message's files are on its Files edge — read `msg-[:Files]->.File`. A message is one of File, Blocks or Buttons.
fieldDocs.Blocks: Slack Block Kit blocks, exactly as in Slack's docs — assembled verbatim and passed through (no wrapping, no typed shape here; a malformed block surfaces as a loud Slack error at run time). For plain buttons write Buttons instead. A press on any control in the blocks arrives on the message's Interactions, its value in the Action's Value: a button's or option's `value`, a picker's pick. Build strings with "${…}" interpolation (never `+`, which is numeric addition). A message is one of File, Blocks or Buttons.
fieldDocs.Buttons: Buttons under the Message text, each `{ Text: "Approve", Value: "approve" }`: Text is the label, Value what a press answers with. Wait for a press with `await msg-[:Interactions]->`; `only(press-[:Actions]->)?.Value` is one of the Values written. Needs Message text; never with File or Blocks.
fieldDocs.Channel: The C… channel id (read-only — a post is written along a Channel's `Messages` edge).
fieldDocs.Topic: A marker of your own for a message with Buttons (`Topic: "lunch-poll"`), so a listen can tell its presses from other messages' presses: `listen to chat-[:Channels]->-[m:Messages WHERE m.Topic == "lunch-poll"]->-[:Interactions]->`. Only a message with Buttons takes one: Slack keeps no other data on a message that comes back with a press, so the Topic is stored as the id of the block its buttons sit in (`lf:<topic>`), and read back from there — on the pressed message and on a listed one alike. It is written only with Buttons, and block ids starting `lf:` are reserved for it: a message whose own Blocks use one is refused.
fieldDocs.Mentions App: Whether the message @-mentions the connected app: `listen to chat-[:Channels]->-[m:Messages WHERE m.`Mentions App` == true]->` runs when somebody asks it something.

Actions.description: The controls used — one for a button press.

Message.description: The message pressed, as Slack sent it with the press: its text, its `Timestamp`, its `Topic`.

Interaction.description: Someone pressing a button (or using another control) on a message — what `await msg-[:Interactions]->` binds, and what a listen on a message's `Interactions` runs on. `Actions` are the controls used, `By` the member who pressed, `Message` the message pressed.

fieldDocs.Id: Names this press (Slack's trigger id).

Action.description: One control used in a press: the value it answered with, and its label.

fieldDocs.Value: What the control answered: a button's Value (one of the Buttons written), a select's chosen option value, a picker's date or time.
fieldDocs.Text: The label of the button, or of the option chosen.

Reaction.description: An emoji reaction added to a message: what a listen on a message's `Reactions` runs on. Walk `Message` to the message it's on, `Channel` to the channel, `Reactor` to the user. Also the reaction WRITE: created along a message's `Reactions` edge, which is how a movement reacts to the message it was handed.

fieldDocs.Emoji: The reaction emoji name (e.g. "thumbsup"), without colons. On a write along `msg-[:Reactions]->`: the single emoji to react with — required.
fieldDocs.Channel: The C… channel id the reaction is in (read-only — walk the `Channel` edge for the Channel node).
fieldDocs.Reactor: The U… id of the user who added the reaction (read-only — walk the `Reactor` edge for the User node).

Channel.description: A Slack channel the connected bot can see. Select one with WHERE on `Name`, then walk its `Messages` (history the bot can read) or `Members`. Listen on its `Messages` for each new message (`listen to chat-[ch:Channels WHERE ch.Name == "deals"]->-[:Messages]->`): each arrives with its channel, so the channel's `Name` is judged on the message itself.

fieldDocs.Name: This workspace has 3 channels — every one of them is offered as a value for this field, so use the field's own values rather than guessing or assuming a channel is missing.

For plain buttons write Buttons instead. A press on any control in the blocks arrives on the message's Interactions, its value in the Action's Value: a button's or option's `value`, a picker's pick. Build strings with "${…}" interpolation (never `+`, which is numeric addition). A message is one of File, Blocks or Buttons.
fieldDocs.Buttons: Buttons under the Message text, each `{ Text: "Approve", Value: "approve" }`: Text is the label, Value what a press answers with. Wait for a press with `await msg-[:Interactions]->`; `only(press-[:Actions]->)?.Value` is one of the Values written. Needs Message text; never with File or Blocks.
fieldDocs.Topic: A marker of your own for a message with Buttons (`Topic: "lunch-poll"`), so a listen can tell its presses from other messages' presses: `listen to chat-[:Channels]->-[m:Messages WHERE m.Topic == "lunch-poll"]->-[:Interactions]->`. Only a message with Buttons takes one: Slack keeps no other data on a message that comes back with a press, so the Topic is stored as the id of the block its buttons sit in (`lf:<topic>`), and read back from there — on the pressed message and on a listed one alike. It is written only with Buttons, and block ids starting `lf:` are reserved for it: a message whose own Blocks use one is refused.

fieldDocs.Emoji: The reaction emoji name (e.g. "thumbsup"), without colons. On a write along `msg-[:Reactions]->`: the single emoji to react with — required.

Interactions.description: A press on one of this message's Buttons (or a control in its Blocks): `await msg-[:Interactions]->` waits for the next one, and `listen to chat-[:Channels]->-[m:Messages WHERE m.Topic == "lunch-poll"]->-[:Interactions]->` runs once per press on any message written with that Topic.

Reactions.description: React to this message with an emoji, or hear a reaction added: `listen to chat-[ch:Channels WHERE ch.Name == "deals"]->-[:Messages]->-[:Reactions]->`. A reaction arrives with its channel, not its message, so a listen narrows it by channel; reading a message's reactions back is not offered (a call per message).

Message.description: A Slack message — what a listen on a channel's `Messages` delivers, whole: read `m.Message` straight off it, reply along its `Replies` edge, react to it along its `Reactions` edge. Created only along an edge: post via a Channel's `Messages` edge, reply via a message's `Replies` edge — the channel and thread come from the parent, never from fields.

fieldDocs.Reactor: The U… id of the user who added the reaction (read-only — walk the `Reactor` edge for the User node).

Channel.description: A Slack channel the connected bot can see. Select one with WHERE on `Name`, then walk its `Messages` (history the bot can read) or `Members`. A WHERE on a message's `Timestamp` narrows the history at Slack rather than after the fetch. Listen on its `Messages` for each new message (`listen to chat-[ch:Channels WHERE ch.Name == "deals"]->-[:Messages]->`): each arrives with its channel, so the channel's `Name` is judged on the message itself.

fieldDocs.Name: This workspace has 3 channels — every one of them is offered as a value for this field, so use the field's own values rather than guessing or assuming a channel is missing.

Replies.description: Send a reply threaded under this message (write-only — the Bot API cannot list replies). The chat and the reply target come from this message.

fieldDocs.Id: Names an arriving message across chats: `<Chat Id>:<Message Id>`, since Telegram numbers a message within its chat. The same on every redelivery.
fieldDocs.Message Id: The Telegram message id, within its chat.
fieldDocs.Text: The message text. On an inbound message: the received text (or the media caption; empty for caption-less media). On a send: the message body — required.
fieldDocs.Chat Id: The id of the chat the message belongs to — the value to send a reply back to, and what a listen narrows to one chat by (`m.`Chat Id` == "42"`).
fieldDocs.Sender Id: The numeric id of the user who sent the message.
fieldDocs.Sender Username: The @username of the sender, when set.

fieldDocs.File Id: The Bot API file id — resolves to the file bytes.

Messages.description: Send a message into this person's private bot chat (write-only — the Bot API cannot list a chat's history). The chat id is the linked user's own id.

Linked User.description: A person who linked Telegram via the connect handshake. Their `Chat Id` is the value a send targets (private chat id = user id).

fieldDocs.Chat Id: The private chat id a send targets (= the Telegram user id).
fieldDocs.Email: The Listen-Fire account email this Telegram user linked as.

Attachments.description: Media attached to the message (zero or more).

Replies.description: Send a reply threaded to this message (write-only — Meta has no read API). The recipient derives from this message; sends only reach a conversation someone opened by messaging the number (Meta's 24-hour service window).

Reactions.description: React to this message with an emoji (write-only).

Typing.description: Show the typing indicator (and mark this message read) while a longer step runs. An action, not a record — nothing is created; do not bind the result.

Message.description: A single inbound WhatsApp message — what a listen on `Messages` delivers, whole: read `e.`Body`` straight off the arrival, reply along its `Replies` edge.

fieldDocs.Message Id: The WhatsApp message id — the value a reply or reaction addresses.
fieldDocs.From: The sender's phone number, digits with the country code first and no plus (`447700900001`): the conversation a message is in, so a listen narrows to one by it.
fieldDocs.To: Inbound: the team's own WhatsApp business number (the message's recipient). On a send: the other party's phone number, derived from the message the write is anchored on (an inbound parent's From, a sent parent's To) — read-only either way.
fieldDocs.Body: The message text. Empty for media-only messages. At least one of Body / File on a send (the Body captions the file).
fieldDocs.File: A file to send (image / PDF / audio / video, routed by content type). At least one of Body / File. Send-side only: a received message's media is on its Attachments edge — read `msg-[:Attachments]->.File`.
fieldDocs.Interactive:
WhatsApp's `interactive` object, exactly as the Cloud API spells it — passed through verbatim (no wrapping, no typed shape here; a malformed object surfaces as a loud WhatsApp error at run time, not at save time). Sending this REPLACES a plain-text send: the interactive type carries its own `body.text`, so the message's words go inside `interactive.body.text`, never in `Body` on the same send. Reply buttons: up to 3, each `{ type: "reply", reply: { id, title } }` (`title` capped at 20 characters); a reply button's tap reaches no run. To make a tap DO something, write a form from the `@lf/forms` adapter (`form = write forms-[:Forms]-> { Title: …, Fields: … }`), send its `form.Url` on a url button (`type: "cta_url"`), and `await form-[:Submissions]->`: the form also asks for anything a person has to fill in, which WhatsApp does not capture at tap time. Build strings with "${…}" interpolation (never `+`, which is numeric addition). Example:
{ type: "cta_url",
  body: { text: "Ship the release?" },
  action: { name: "cta_url", parameters: { display_text: "Answer", url: "${form.Url}" } } }
fieldDocs.Profile Name: The sender's WhatsApp profile display name.
fieldDocs.Timestamp: When the message was received (ISO-8601), when known.

fieldDocs.Emoji: The reaction emoji. Inbound: empty when the reaction was removed. On a write along msg-[:Reactions]->: the single emoji to react with — required.
fieldDocs.Reacted Message Id: The message the reaction is on.

Location.description: Someone shared a location with the team number. What a listen on `Locations` delivers.

fieldDocs.Name: The place name, when the sender picked one.

Typing.description: The typing-indicator action, written along a message's `Typing` edge (`write msg-[:Typing]-> {}` — no fields; Meta's API is on-only, so there is no off to write). An action, not a record: nothing is created and nothing reads back. WhatsApp clears the indicator itself when your reply sends, or after ~25 seconds.

Event.description: Something that happened to the host’s runs, waits or releases. `Kind` says which.

fieldDocs.Event Id: Names the event: the same on every poll that finds it.
fieldDocs.Kind: Which thing happened. A listen names the kinds it wants: `e.Kind == "Run Failed"`, or `e.Kind IN [...]`.
fieldDocs.Automation: The program the event is about (its movement); empty when it concerns none.
fieldDocs.Run Id: The run the event is about; empty when it concerns none.
fieldDocs.Version: The release involved; empty when none is.
fieldDocs.Reason: What happened, in words: for a failed run, why it failed.
fieldDocs.Url: A link to where a person sees it; empty where the host has no such page.
fieldDocs.Adapter: For a wait that lost its record: the module its record is in. Empty on every other kind.
fieldDocs.Edge: For a wait that lost its record: the edge it waits on. For an arrival not judged: the edge it arrived on. Empty on every other kind.
fieldDocs.Record Id: For a wait that lost its record: the deleted record’s id. For an arrival not judged: the record that arrived. Empty on every other kind.
fieldDocs.Listen: For an arrival not judged: the listen that could not judge it, as the host names it. Empty on every other kind.
fieldDocs.Delivery Id: For an arrival not judged: the delivery it came in, which the host keeps for a while (on listen-fire `deliveries.retainDays`, 14 days by default); empty when the host kept none. Empty on every other kind.
fieldDocs.Arrival Id: For an arrival not judged: the arrival, as the listen names it (its edge, record, identity and version). Empty on every other kind.
fieldDocs.Attempt: For an arrival not judged: 0 when it was delivered, one more for each replay (`listen-fire listens replay`) that still could not judge it. 0 on every other kind.

Pull Requests.description: Pull requests, open and closed, newest first. `State` reaches GitHub; other filters run over what comes back, so pin `State` == "open" on a busy repository.

Issues.description: Issues (not pull requests), open and closed, newest first. `State`, `Author`, a label in `Label Names`, an assignee in `Assignees` and an `Updated At` lower bound reach GitHub.

Repository.description: A repository: its pull requests and its issues.

fieldDocs.Full Name: `owner/name`. An `==` in a `Repositories` WHERE fetches that repository directly.

Repository.description: The repository the thread is in.

Pull Request.description: The pull request it is about; nothing when `Subject Type` is not `PullRequest`.

Issue.description: The issue it is about; nothing when `Subject Type` is not `Issue`.

Notification.description: A notification thread: why you were told (`Reason`), what about (`Title`, `Subject Type`), and where. Walk `Pull Request` or `Issue` for the subject itself.

fieldDocs.Id: The thread id.
fieldDocs.Reason: Why you got it (`review_requested`, `mention`, `assign`, …). A thread’s reason can change as it moves.
fieldDocs.Participating: Whether you take part in the thread or are mentioned in it: GitHub tells only by its `participating` filter, so every thread, walked or heard, is stamped with it from one extra call (made only when there are threads).
fieldDocs.Title: The subject’s title (`subject.title`).

Comments.description: The conversation, oldest first (a pull request’s are its issue comments, not its review comments). Comment here: `write pr-[:Comments]-> { Body: "…" }`.

Labels.description: The labels it carries. Add one: `write issue-[:Labels]-> { Name: "bug" }` (GitHub creates a label the repository does not have yet; adding one it already carries changes nothing).

Pull Request.description: A pull request. Comment on it along `Comments`; label it along `Labels`.

fieldDocs.Author: The login of who opened it (`user.login`).
fieldDocs.Label Names: The names of its labels; `Labels` are the labels themselves.
fieldDocs.Requested Reviewers: The logins asked to review it.

Comments.description: The conversation, oldest first (a pull request’s are its issue comments, not its review comments). Comment here: `write pr-[:Comments]-> { Body: "…" }`.

Labels.description: The labels it carries. Add one: `write issue-[:Labels]-> { Name: "bug" }` (GitHub creates a label the repository does not have yet; adding one it already carries changes nothing).

Issue.description: An issue. Comment on it along `Comments`; label it along `Labels`.

fieldDocs.Author: The login of who opened it (`user.login`).
fieldDocs.Label Names: The names of its labels; `Labels` are the labels themselves.
fieldDocs.State Reason: Why it was closed (`completed`, `not_planned`, …), or reopened.

Comment.description: A comment in a pull request’s or an issue’s conversation.

Label.description: A label on a pull request or an issue.

forms.description: A form at a link, answered once. A write makes it; the node the write names in Fields says what it asks, and its answer lands on the form’s Submissions, typed by that node.

Submission.description: An answer to a form: the fields of the node the form asked for, and its Id.

fieldDocs.Id: The answer’s id: a form takes one, so its form’s.

Submissions.description: The form’s one answer, with the fields of the node the write named.

fieldDocs.Title: What the form asks, shown above its fields.
fieldDocs.Fields: The node the form asks for (`Fields: Refund`): its fields are the form’s, and its submissions have them.

label_added.changed: a label removed from a message and added again now runs the listen again, where 0.12 ran it once per message and label

Attachments.description: Files attached to the message (zero or more). Listing them is free — the bytes are fetched only when `File` is read.

Replies.description: Write here to reply to this message inside its conversation. The thread, the `Re:` subject and the `In-Reply-To` / `References` headers all come from this parent — a reply names only what it says (`Body`), and may override `Subject`, `To` or `Cc`. Not readable: this connection sends into a conversation, it does not read one back.

Drafts.description: Write here to keep a reply to this message unsent, for a person to finish. Threaded exactly as a reply along `Replies` is.

Message.description: One message in the mailbox — who sent it, what it says, and what came attached. Read `Body` for what it says without caring which format arrived. A Message written along the mailbox’s `Messages` edge is a NEW message; a Message written along another message’s `Replies` edge is a reply, and its thread, its `Re:` subject and its reply headers all come from that parent rather than from fields. A send sets `To`, `Subject`, `Body` (and `HTML Body` / `Files` when they apply); a reply needs nothing but a body.

fieldDocs.Message Id: Gmail's own id for the message.
fieldDocs.Thread Id: The conversation this message belongs to. Read-only: a reply joins a conversation by being written along that message’s `Replies` edge, never by naming its thread.
fieldDocs.Subject: On a read, the subject line; a WHERE reaches Gmail as a `subject:` search — `=` and `contains` alike, since Gmail matches words rather than whole strings, and the engine then narrows `=` to an exact match. On a send, the subject to use; a reply that leaves it unset gets the parent’s subject with `Re:` in front.
fieldDocs.From: The "From" header whole, display name included ("Rita Okoye" <rita@…>). Read-only on a send too: mail always leaves as the connected mailbox, which is the only address this deployment is allowed to be. A WHERE reaches Gmail as a `from:` search.
fieldDocs.To: The addresses on the "To" header — a list, each either a bare address or `"Name" <address>`. Required on a new message; a reply that leaves it unset answers whoever sent the parent. A WHERE reaches Gmail as a `to:` search.
fieldDocs.Cc: The addresses on the "Cc" header, written the same way as `To`. A reply does NOT inherit the parent’s Cc — copy people in deliberately. A WHERE reaches Gmail as a `cc:` search.
fieldDocs.Date: When Gmail received the message. Bounds reach the search as `after:` / `before:`, which are whole-second and inclusive over there — the engine narrows the edges.
fieldDocs.Body: On a read, the normalised body — plain text, derived from the HTML when only HTML arrived; use this for "what it says", and a `contains` reaches Gmail as a word search. On a send, the plain-text body. Every send needs a `Body` or an `HTML Body`.
fieldDocs.Plain Body: The plain-text alternative exactly as it arrived, or nothing when the message was HTML only. Read-only — `Body` is what a send sets.
fieldDocs.HTML Body: The HTML alternative. Set it alongside `Body` on a send and the message goes out as both, so a reader that cannot show HTML still sees the text.
fieldDocs.Files: Files to attach to a message being sent — a list of file values the run already holds (an attachment read off another message, a document a movement produced). Send-side only: the files on a RECEIVED message are on its `Attachments` edge.
fieldDocs.Labels: Label names — a user label as the mailbox calls it (Deals), Gmail’s own in capitals (INBOX, UNREAD, IMPORTANT), in a walk and in a listen alike. A WHERE reaches the search as `label:`, and an OR of `CONTAINS` hears mail carrying any of them (`m.Labels CONTAINS "Deals" OR m.Labels CONTAINS "Hiring"`). This connection can read them and can never set one.
fieldDocs.Has Attachments: Whether walking `Attachments` would find anything — true without fetching a single byte.
fieldDocs.Query: A Gmail search written exactly as in Gmail’s own search box (`m.Query == "from:@acme.com has:attachment"`): what is searched for comes back. Compared with `==` only. Read, it is the search the message was found by (what its listen or walk compared it with), and nothing on a message found otherwise.

Labels.note: it holds label names (`Deals`) where it held label ids (`Label_12`); Gmail’s own labels (`INBOX`, `UNREAD`) are spelled as before

Message.description: The message that was labelled, whole: walk its `Attachments`, or reply along its `Replies`.

Labeling.description: Each label added to a message already in the mailbox — a person filing mail, or a filter doing it later: what a listen hears, never a list to read. Narrow it by `Label` (a label by its name) or `Label Type` (`"user"` for the mailbox’s own labels), and by `Query`.

fieldDocs.Id: This addition: the message, the label and the moment in the mailbox’s history it was added.
fieldDocs.Label: The label that was added, by name: a user label as the mailbox calls it (Deals), Gmail’s own in capitals (INBOX, STARRED), as `Labels` on a message. A listen names it the same way (`l.Label == "Deals"`); a label the mailbox does not have fails the listen, naming the ones it has.
fieldDocs.Label Type: `user` for the mailbox’s own labels, `system` for Gmail’s (inbox, unread, starred, important, sent, draft, spam, trash, chat, the category tabs), which change as mail is read and filed.
fieldDocs.Query: A Gmail search written exactly as in Gmail’s own search box (`m.Query == "from:@acme.com has:attachment"`): what is searched for comes back. Compared with `==` only. Read, it is the search the message was found by (what its listen or walk compared it with), and nothing on a message found otherwise.
fieldDocs.Message Id: Gmail's own id for the message.
fieldDocs.Thread Id: The conversation this message belongs to. Read-only: a reply joins a conversation by being written along that message’s `Replies` edge, never by naming its thread.

Draft.description: A message kept unsent in the mailbox. A Draft written along the mailbox’s `Drafts` edge is kept unsent for a person to finish; along a message’s `Drafts` edge it is a reply kept unsent, threaded as a reply is. Drafts work only where the mailbox was signed in with drafts enabled (the `gmail_drafts` credential). Every field is optional: a person finishes the draft. The write hands back its `Id`, `Message Id` and `Thread Id`.

fieldDocs.Id: Gmail's id for the draft (not its message's).
fieldDocs.Message Id: The id of the message the draft holds.
fieldDocs.Thread Id: The conversation the draft belongs to: its parent’s, on a reply draft.
fieldDocs.To: The addresses on the "To" header. A reply draft that leaves it unset answers whoever sent the parent.
fieldDocs.Subject: The subject line; a reply draft that leaves it unset gets the parent’s with `Re:` in front.
fieldDocs.Files: Files to attach — a list of file values the run already holds.

Attachment.description: One file on a message. Gmail serves the bytes from their own endpoint, so the name, type and size cost nothing and only `File` costs a fetch.

fieldDocs.File: The bytes themselves — fetched when read, so a message whose files nobody opens costs nothing.

Attachments.description: Files attached to the message (zero or more). Listing them is free — the bytes are fetched only when `File` is read.

Replies.description: Write here to reply to this message inside its conversation. The thread, the `Re:` subject and the `In-Reply-To` / `References` headers all come from this parent — a reply names only what it says (`Body`), and may override `Subject`, `To` or `Cc`. Not readable: this connection sends into a conversation, it does not read one back.

Drafts.description: Write here to keep a reply to this message unsent, for a person to finish. Threaded exactly as a reply along `Replies` is.

Changes.description: What happens to a Company in the graph, each change once: created, updated (`Changed Fields` names what moved), deleted.
What happens to a Person in the graph, each change once: created, updated (`Changed Fields` names what moved), deleted.
What happens to a Support Ticket in the graph, each change once: created, updated (`Changed Fields` names what moved), deleted.

Record.description: The record as it is now, read from the graph: none once it is deleted.

Company Change.description: A change to a Company in the graph: what happened (`Kind`), which properties and edges moved (`Changed Fields`), and the record as the change left it (`Current`, absent once deleted; test it present before reading through it: `exists(c.Current) AND c.Current.Status == "Open"`). Walk `Record` for the record as it is now.

fieldDocs.Id: Names the change: the same each time the graph reports it.
fieldDocs.Changed Fields: The properties and edges the change moved, by name: every one a created record was given, none for a deleted one.
fieldDocs.Record Id: The graph's id for the record, a deleted one's too.
fieldDocs.Current: The record as the change left it, every property by name. Absent when it was deleted.

@lf/web/vc_url_retrieval.description: Discover, classify, and fetch URLs in a message. Emits one ephemeral Url record per fetched resource.
@lf/web/vc_url_retrieval.name: vc_url_retrieval

@lf/web/fetch_url.description: Fetch one named URL and hand back its content. Emits a single ephemeral Url record.
@lf/web/fetch_url.name: fetch_url

@lf/web/linkedin_enrichment.description: For an identified person without a LinkedIn profile, find their profile — searching the web for it unless the person already carries the address — and attach the profile URL and page content.
@lf/web/linkedin_enrichment.name: linkedin_enrichment

@lf/web/linkedin_research.description: From a LinkedIn profile address, research what that person is currently doing — their role, their organisation, and their recent public activity — and attach a summary, a confidence, the sources it rests on, and the passages found about them. Passages with no summary mean the research could not confirm anything beyond that text.
@lf/web/linkedin_research.name: linkedin_research

@lf/web/web_research.description: Find a company's own website from its name and what a message said about it, and fetch it. Stands down for a record that already carries a link.
@lf/web/web_research.name: web_research

@lf/web/research.description: Research one person or company from whatever the record carries — a name, a line of context, a website, a profile address — and attach a dossier that answers what you ask, with its sources and a confidence.
@lf/web/research.name: research

@lf/web/render.description: Draw text or HTML as a PDF file with the host's browser. HTML keeps its layout; plain text is wrapped in a page. Refuses when the host has no browser.
@lf/web/render.name: render

@lf/pdf/render.description: Draw plain text as a PDF file. A character the default writer has no glyph for prints as "?", with a warning on the run.
@lf/pdf/render.name: render
